# gh-1551: Slim the 2h schedule tick: skip the full CI gate when no commits landed since the last tag

## Description

## Problem

gh-1537 (#1541) retired the post-merge main CI run — releases now arm on the 2h coalesce schedule (cron `23 */2 * * *`). But the scheduled tick runs the **full quality gate (~35-40 min wall)** every 2 hours **even when zero commits landed on main since the last `v*` tag** — pure waste against the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle.

Observed: run 38147581679 (2026-10-11 14:32Z, event=schedule, main) — full gate with nothing new to release.

## Proposal

Add a cheap pre-check job (`release-pending`): compare `origin/main` HEAD against the latest `v*` tag — if no new commits, the whole downstream (quality-gate legs, release) skips in seconds.

- The gate graph keys off `needs` — wire the existing `changes`-style pattern: every gate leg adds `release-pending` to its needs/condition, or (simpler) a single early `exit` job that the `quality-gate` aggregator requires.
- Tag pushes, `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) stay untouched — they must never be skipped by this check.
- Cost: one API call + `git rev-list`, ~10-30s per empty tick.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Empty tick (no commits since last tag): run completes green in <1 min, release job skipped explicitly (visible in the run, not silently absent).
- [ ] Non-empty tick: behaves exactly as today (full gate → tag cut on green).
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) and tag/`release` events unaffected — regression-pinned.
- [ ] ci.yml comment block updated: the schedule is the release arming mechanism, empty ticks short-circuit.

Context: #1537 (post-merge main CI retirement), #1538 (slim nightly), ci.yml `schedule:` + `release` job comments.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg is
#               the only macOS test surface)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Added a `release-pending` pre-check job to ci.yml (gh-1551): on schedule ticks it compares main HEAD against the latest semver `v*` tag (`git rev-list --count`, ~10-30 s) and exports a `pending` output; every gate leg (30 jobs — classifier, all quality-gate legs, `quality-gate`, `step-timings`, `release`) ANDs `needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` into its `if`. - **Boolean safety**: existing `||`-chained path conditions were wrapped in parens before ANDing the guard (`&&` binds tighter than `||`).
- **Comment blocks updated**: the `schedule:` cron comment and the gate-graph overview now document that the schedule is the release arming mechanism and empty ticks short-circuit.
- Regression-pinned by a new workflow-shape guard test following the repo's never-again pattern (same style as `ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart   # new gh-1551 pins (7 tests)
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart  # no regressions
```
Full unit suite verified locally: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → 10272 passed, 0 failed.

<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[schedule cron 23 */2] --> RP[release-pending]
  PUSH[v* tag push] --> RP
  REL[release: published] --> RP
  DISP[workflow_dispatch dryRun/dispatch] --> RP
  RP -->|pending=true| CHANGES[changes classifier + full quality gate]
  RP -->|pending=false: empty tick| SKIP[all legs SKIPPED explicitly]
  CHANGES --> QG[quality-gate always()]
  QG --> RELJOB[release: tag cut]
  SKIP --> RELJOB
```

# gh-1551: Slim the 2h schedule tick: skip the full CI gate when no commits landed since the last tag

## Description

## Problem

gh-1537 (#1541) retired the post-merge main CI run — releases now arm on the 2h coalesce schedule (cron `23 */2 * * *`). But the scheduled tick runs the **full quality gate (~35-40 min wall)** every 2 hours **even when zero commits landed on main since the last `v*` tag** — pure waste against the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle.

Observed: run 38147581679 (2026-10-11 14:32Z, event=schedule, main) — full gate with nothing new to release.

## Proposal

Add a cheap pre-check job (`release-pending`): compare `origin/main` HEAD against the latest `v*` tag — if no new commits, the whole downstream (quality-gate legs, release) skips in seconds.

- The gate graph keys off `needs` — wire the existing `changes`-style pattern: every gate leg adds `release-pending` to its needs/condition, or (simpler) a single early `exit` job that the `quality-gate` aggregator requires.
- Tag pushes, `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) stay untouched — they must never be skipped by this check.
- Cost: one API call + `git rev-list`, ~10-30s per empty tick.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Empty tick (no commits since last tag): run completes green in <1 min, release job skipped explicitly (visible in the run, not silently absent).
- [ ] Non-empty tick: behaves exactly as today (full gate → tag cut on green).
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) and tag/`release` events unaffected — regression-pinned.
- [ ] ci.yml comment block updated: the schedule is the release arming mechanism, empty ticks short-circuit.

Context: #1537 (post-merge main CI retirement), #1538 (slim nightly), ci.yml `schedule:` + `release` job comments.

# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1553
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1553
- **Title**: gh-1551 Slim the 2h schedule tick: skip the full CI gate when no commits landed since the last tag
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1551` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +459
- **Deletions**: -51
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T15:42:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T16:04:13Z

## PR Description

Closes #1551
### What changed
Added a `release-pending` pre-check job to ci.yml (gh-1551): on schedule ticks it compares main HEAD against the latest semver `v*` tag (`git rev-list --count`, ~10-30 s) and exports a `pending` output; every gate leg (30 jobs — classifier, all quality-gate legs, `quality-gate`, `step-timings`, `release`) ANDs `needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` into its `if`. An empty tick now skips the whole graph in seconds with every leg visibly SKIPPED and the run green; a non-empty tick falls through to the exact gh-1537 graph.

### Key decisions
- **Fail-open**: `pending` defaults to `true` and flips to `false` only in the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check degrades to the full gate with a `::warning::`, never silently suppresses a release; the check never `exit 1`s.
- **Untouched arms (AC3)**: tag pushes, `release: published` and both dispatch arms short-circuit to `pending=true` before the checkout (the fetch is `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'` — they don't even pay it); the tag/release chain (`publish`, `binaries`, `integration`, …) carries zero `release-pending` references — pinned by test.
- **Boolean safety**: existing `||`-chained path conditions were wrapped in parens before ANDing the guard (`&&` binds tighter than `||`).
- **Comment blocks updated**: the `schedule:` cron comment and the gate-graph overview now document that the schedule is the release arming mechanism and empty ticks short-circuit.
- Regression-pinned by a new workflow-shape guard test following the repo's never-again pattern (same style as `ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart   # new gh-1551 pins (7 tests)
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart  # no regressions
```
Full unit suite verified locally: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → 10272 passed, 0 failed.

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[schedule cron 23 */2] --> RP[release-pending]
  PUSH[v* tag push] --> RP
  REL[release: published] --> RP
  DISP[workflow_dispatch dryRun/dispatch] --> RP
  RP -->|pending=true| CHANGES[changes classifier + full quality gate]
  RP -->|pending=false: empty tick| SKIP[all legs SKIPPED explicitly]
  CHANGES --> QG[quality-gate always()]
  QG --> RELJOB[release: tag cut]
  SKIP --> RELJOB
```
</details>

# gh-1551: Slim the 2h schedule tick: skip the full CI gate when no commits landed since the last tag

## Description

## Problem

gh-1537 (#1541) retired the post-merge main CI run — releases now arm on the 2h coalesce schedule (cron `23 */2 * * *`). But the scheduled tick runs the **full quality gate (~35-40 min wall)** every 2 hours **even when zero commits landed on main since the last `v*` tag** — pure waste against the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle.

Observed: run 38147581679 (2026-10-11 14:32Z, event=schedule, main) — full gate with nothing new to release.

## Proposal

Add a cheap pre-check job (`release-pending`): compare `origin/main` HEAD against the latest `v*` tag — if no new commits, the whole downstream (quality-gate legs, release) skips in seconds.

- The gate graph keys off `needs` — wire the existing `changes`-style pattern: every gate leg adds `release-pending` to its needs/condition, or (simpler) a single early `exit` job that the `quality-gate` aggregator requires.
- Tag pushes, `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) stay untouched — they must never be skipped by this check.
- Cost: one API call + `git rev-list`, ~10-30s per empty tick.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Empty tick (no commits since last tag): run completes green in <1 min, release job skipped explicitly (visible in the run, not silently absent).
- [ ] Non-empty tick: behaves exactly as today (full gate → tag cut on green).
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) and tag/`release` events unaffected — regression-pinned.
- [ ] ci.yml comment block updated: the schedule is the release arming mechanism, empty ticks short-circuit.

Context: #1537 (post-merge main CI retirement), #1538 (slim nightly), ci.yml `schedule:` + `release` job comments.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg is
#               the only macOS test surface)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
----
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, quality-gate]

## PR Description

Closes #1551
### What changed
Added a `release-pending` pre-check job to ci.yml (gh-1551): on schedule ticks it compares main HEAD against the latest semver `v*` tag (`git rev-list --count`, ~10-30 s) and exports a `pending` output; every gate leg (30 jobs — classifier, all quality-gate legs, `quality-gate`, `step-timings`, `release`) ANDs `needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` into its `if`. An empty tick now skips the whole graph in seconds with every leg visibly SKIPPED and the run green; a non-empty tick falls through to the exact gh-1537 graph.

### Key decisions
- **Fail-open**: `pending` defaults to `true` and flips to `false` only in the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check degrades to the full gate with a `::warning::`, never silently suppresses a release; the check never `exit 1`s.
- **Untouched arms (AC3)**: tag pushes, `release: published` and both dispatch arms short-circuit to `pending=true` before the checkout (the fetch is `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'` — they don't even pay it); the tag/release chain (`publish`, `binaries`, `integration`, …) carries zero `release-pending` references — pinned by test.
- **Boolean safety**: existing `||`-chained path conditions were wrapped in parens before ANDing the guard (`&&` binds tighter than `||`).
- **Comment blocks updated**: the `schedule:` cron comment and the gate-graph overview now document that the schedule is the release arming mechanism and empty ticks short-circuit.
- Regression-pinned by a new workflow-shape guard test following the repo's never-again pattern (same style as `ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart   # new gh-1551 pins (7 tests)
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart  # no regressions
```
Full unit suite verified locally: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → 10272 passed, 0 failed.

```mermaid

  TICK[schedule cron 23 */2] --> RP[release-pending]
  PUSH[v* tag push] --> RP
  REL[release: published] --> RP
  DISP[workflow_dispatch dryRun/dispatch] --> RP
  RP -->|pending=true| CHANGES[changes classifier + full quality gate]
  RP -->|pending=false: empty tick| SKIP[all legs SKIPPED explicitly]
  CHANGES --> QG[quality-gate always()]

# gh-1551: Slim the 2h schedule tick: skip the full CI gate when no commits landed since the last tag

## Description

## Problem

gh-1537 (#1541) retired the post-merge main CI run — releases now arm on the 2h coalesce schedule (cron `23 */2 * * *`). But the scheduled tick runs the **full quality gate (~35-40 min wall)** every 2 hours **even when zero commits landed on main since the last `v*` tag** — pure waste against the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle.

Observed: run 38147581679 (2026-10-11 14:32Z, event=schedule, main) — full gate with nothing new to release.

## Proposal

Add a cheap pre-check job (`release-pending`): compare `origin/main` HEAD against the latest `v*` tag — if no new commits, the whole downstream (quality-gate legs, release) skips in seconds.

- The gate graph keys off `needs` — wire the existing `changes`-style pattern: every gate leg adds `release-pending` to its needs/condition, or (simpler) a single early `exit` job that the `quality-gate` aggregator requires.
- Tag pushes, `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) stay untouched — they must never be skipped by this check.
- Cost: one API call + `git rev-list`, ~10-30s per empty tick.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Empty tick (no commits since last tag): run completes green in <1 min, release job skipped explicitly (visible in the run, not silently absent).
- [ ] Non-empty tick: behaves exactly as today (full gate → tag cut on green).
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) and tag/`release` events unaffected — regression-pinned.
- [ ] ci.yml comment block updated: the schedule is the release arming mechanism, empty ticks short-circuit.

Context: #1537 (post-merge main CI retirement), #1538 (slim nightly), ci.yml `schedule:` + `release` job comments.

## Machine jobs

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg is
#               the only macOS test surface)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)

watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
----
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T16:04:13Z

## PR Description

Closes #1551
### What changed
Added a `release-pending` pre-check job to ci.yml (gh-1551): on schedule ticks it compares main HEAD against the latest semver `v*` tag (`git rev-list --count`, ~10-30 s) and exports a `pending` output; every gate leg (30 jobs — classifier, all quality-gate legs, `quality-gate`, `step-timings`, `release`) ANDs `needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` into its `if`. An empty tick now skips the whole graph in seconds with every leg visibly SKIPPED and the run green; a non-empty tick falls through to the exact gh-1537 graph.

### Key decisions
- **Fail-open**: `pending` defaults to `true` and flips to `false` only in the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check degrades to the full gate with a `::warning::`, never silently suppresses a release; the check never `exit 1`s.
- **Untouched arms (AC3)**: tag pushes, `release: published` and both dispatch arms short-circuit to `pending=true` before the checkout (the fetch is `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'` — they don't even pay it); the tag/release chain (`publish`, `binaries`, `integration`, …) carries zero `release-pending` references — pinned by test.
- **Boolean safety**: existing `||`-chained path conditions were wrapped in parens before ANDing the guard (`&&` binds tighter than `||`).
- **Comment blocks updated**: the `schedule:` cron comment and the gate-graph overview now document that the schedule is the release arming mechanism and empty ticks short-circuit.
- Regression-pinned by a new workflow-shape guard test following the repo's never-again pattern (same style as `ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart   # new gh-1551 pins (7 tests)
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart  # no regressions
```
Full unit suite verified locally: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → 10272 passed, 0 failed.

<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[schedule cron 23 */2] --> RP[release-pending]
  PUSH[v* tag push] --> RP
  REL[release: published] --> RP
  DISP[workflow_dispatch dryRun/dispatch] --> RP
  RP -->|pending=true| CHANGES[changes classifier + full quality gate]
  RP -->|pending=false: empty tick| SKIP[all legs SKIPPED explicitly]
  CHANGES --> QG[quality-gate always()]
  QG --> RELJOB[release: tag cut]
  SKIP --> RELJOB
```

# gh-1551: Slim the 2h schedule tick: skip the full CI gate when no commits landed since the last tag

## Description

## Problem

gh-1537 (#1541) retired the post-merge main CI run — releases now arm on the 2h coalesce schedule (cron `23 */2 * * *`). But the scheduled tick runs the **full quality gate (~35-40 min wall)** every 2 hours **even when zero commits landed on main since the last `v*` tag** — pure waste against the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle.

Observed: run 38147581679 (2026-10-11 14:32Z, event=schedule, main) — full gate with nothing new to release.

## Proposal

Add a cheap pre-check job (`release-pending`): compare `origin/main` HEAD against the latest `v*` tag — if no new commits, the whole downstream (quality-gate legs, release) skips in seconds.

- The gate graph keys off `needs` — wire the existing `changes`-style pattern: every gate leg adds `release-pending` to its needs/condition, or (simpler) a single early `exit` job that the `quality-gate` aggregator requires.
- Tag pushes, `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) stay untouched — they must never be skipped by this check.
- Cost: one API call + `git rev-list`, ~10-30s per empty tick.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Empty tick (no commits since last tag): run completes green in <1 min, release job skipped explicitly (visible in the run, not silently absent).
- [ ] Non-empty tick: behaves exactly as today (full gate → tag cut on green).
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) and tag/`release` events unaffected — regression-pinned.
- [ ] ci.yml comment block updated: the schedule is the release arming mechanism, empty ticks short-circuit.

Context: #1537 (post-merge main CI retirement), #1538 (slim nightly), ci.yml `schedule:` + `release` job comments.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38149342319) · started 14:59 · done 15:43 ✅

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg is
#               the only macOS test surface)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate
#                in seconds (see the job comment below)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.

blocks.text:
watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
----
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

    # gated dispatches only. Every armed tick cuts an annotated tag
    # (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on

    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and
    # CI stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish
    # time. The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because
    # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries
    # jobs (gh-1172); the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no
    # branch push), but remains the release-path actor (gh-1402).
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate

    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun

## PR Description

Closes #1551
### What changed
Added a `release-pending` pre-check job to ci.yml (gh-1551): on schedule ticks it compares main HEAD against the latest semver `v*` tag (`git rev-list --count`, ~10-30 s) and exports a `pending` output; every gate leg (30 jobs — classifier, all quality-gate legs, `quality-gate`, `step-timings`, `release`) ANDs `needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` into its `if`. An empty tick now skips the whole graph in seconds with every leg visibly SKIPPED and the run green; a non-empty tick falls through to the exact gh-1537 graph.

### Key decisions
- **Fail-open**: `pending` defaults to `true` and flips to `false` only in the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check degrades to the full gate with a `::warning::`, never silently suppresses a release; the check never `exit 1`s.
- **Untouched arms (AC3)**: tag pushes, `release: published` and both dispatch arms short-circuit to `pending=true` before the checkout (the fetch is `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'` — they don't even pay it); the tag/release chain (`publish`, `binaries`, `integration`, …) carries zero `release-pending` references — pinned by test.
- **Boolean safety**: existing `||`-chained path conditions were wrapped in parens before ANDing the guard (`&&` binds tighter than `||`).
- **Comment blocks updated**: the `schedule:` cron comment and the gate-graph overview now document that the schedule is the release arming mechanism and empty ticks short-circuit.
- Regression-pinned by a new workflow-shape guard test following the repo's never-again pattern (same style as `ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart   # new gh-1551 pins (7 tests)
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart  # no regressions

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[schedule cron 23 */2] --> RP[release-pending]
  PUSH[v* tag push] --> RP
  REL[release: published] --> RP
  DISP[workflow_dispatch dryRun/dispatch] --> RP
  RP -->|pending=true| CHANGES[changes classifier + full quality gate]
  RP -->|pending=false: empty tick| SKIP[all legs SKIPPED explicitly]
  CHANGES --> QG[quality-gate always()]

# gh-1551: Slim the 2h schedule tick: skip the full CI gate when no commits landed since the last tag

## Description

## Problem

gh-1537 (#1541) retired the post-merge main CI run — releases now arm on the 2h coalesce schedule (cron `23 */2 * * *`). But the scheduled tick runs the **full quality gate (~35-40 min wall)** every 2 hours **even when zero commits landed on main since the last `v*` tag** — pure waste against the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle.

Observed: run 38147581679 (2026-10-11 14:32Z, event=schedule, main) — full gate with nothing new to release.

## Proposal

Add a cheap pre-check job (`release-pending`): compare `origin/main` HEAD against the latest `v*` tag — if no new commits, the whole downstream (quality-gate legs, release) skips in seconds.

- The gate graph keys off `needs` — wire the existing `changes`-style pattern: every gate leg adds `release-pending` to its needs/condition, or (simpler) a single early `exit` job that the `quality-gate` aggregator requires.
- Tag pushes, `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) stay untouched — they must never be skipped by this check.
- Cost: one API call + `git rev-list`, ~10-30s per empty tick.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Empty tick (no commits since last tag): run completes green in <1 min, release job skipped explicitly (visible in the run, not silently absent).
- [ ] Non-empty tick: behaves exactly as today (full gate → tag cut on green).
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) and tag/`release` events unaffected — regression-pinned.
- [ ] ci.yml comment block updated: the schedule is the release arming mechanism, empty ticks short-circuit.

Context: #1537 (post-merge main CI retirement), #1538 (slim nightly), ci.yml `schedule:` + `release` job comments.

## Machine jobs

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

blocks.text:
watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
----
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

    # CI stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish

- **Additions**: +459
- **Deletions**: -51
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T15:42:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T16:04:13Z

## PR Description

Closes #1551
### What changed
Added a `release-pending` pre-check job to ci.yml (gh-1551): on schedule ticks it compares main HEAD against the latest semver `v*` tag (`git rev-list --count`, ~10-30 s) and exports a `pending` output; every gate leg (30 jobs — classifier, all quality-gate legs, `quality-gate`, `step-timings`, `release`) ANDs `needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'` into its `if`. An empty tick now skips the whole graph in seconds with every leg visibly SKIPPED and the run green; a non-empty tick falls through to the exact gh-1537 graph.

### Key decisions
- **Fail-open**: `pending` defaults to `true` and flips to `false` only in the zero-commits branch — a flaky pre-check degrades to the full gate with a `::warning::`, never silently suppresses a release; the check never `exit 1`s.
- **Untouched arms (AC3)**: tag pushes, `release: published` and both dispatch arms short-circuit to `pending=true` before the checkout (the fetch is `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'` — they don't even pay it); the tag/release chain (`publish`, `binaries`, `integration`, …) carries zero `release-pending` references — pinned by test.
- **Boolean safety**: existing `||`-chained path conditions were wrapped in parens before ANDing the guard (`&&` binds tighter than `||`).
- **Comment blocks updated**: the `schedule:` cron comment and the gate-graph overview now document that the schedule is the release arming mechanism and empty ticks short-circuit.
- Regression-pinned by a new workflow-shape guard test following the repo's never-again pattern (same style as `ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart   # new gh-1551 pins (7 tests)
dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/ci_main_push_retired_test.dart  # no regressions
```
Full unit suite verified locally: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → 10272 passed, 0 failed.

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TICK[schedule cron 23 */2] --> RP[release-pending]
  PUSH[v* tag push] --> RP
  REL[release: published] --> RP
  DISP[workflow_dispatch dryRun/dispatch] --> RP
  RP -->|pending=true| CHANGES[changes classifier + full quality gate]
  RP -->|pending=false: empty tick| SKIP[all legs SKIPPED explicitly]
  CHANGES --> QG[quality-gate always()]
  QG --> RELJOB[release: tag cut]
  SKIP --> RELJOB
```
</details>

# gh-1551: Slim the 2h schedule tick: skip the full CI gate when no commits landed since the last tag

## Description

## Problem

gh-1537 (#1541) retired the post-merge main CI run — releases now arm on the 2h coalesce schedule (cron `23 */2 * * *`). But the scheduled tick runs the **full quality gate (~35-40 min wall)** every 2 hours **even when zero commits landed on main since the last `v*` tag** — pure waste against the shift-left / zero-duplicate-runs principle.

Observed: run 38147581679 (2026-10-11 14:32Z, event=schedule, main) — full gate with nothing new to release.

## Proposal

Add a cheap pre-check job (`release-pending`): compare `origin/main` HEAD against the latest `v*` tag — if no new commits, the whole downstream (quality-gate legs, release) skips in seconds.

- The gate graph keys off `needs` — wire the existing `changes`-style pattern: every gate leg adds `release-pending` to its needs/condition, or (simpler) a single early `exit` job that the `quality-gate` aggregator requires.
- Tag pushes, `release: published` events and both dispatch arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) stay untouched — they must never be skipped by this check.
- Cost: one API call + `git rev-list`, ~10-30s per empty tick.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Empty tick (no commits since last tag): run completes green in <1 min, release job skipped explicitly (visible in the run, not silently absent).
- [ ] Non-empty tick: behaves exactly as today (full gate → tag cut on green).
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` arms (`releaseDryRun`, `releaseDispatch`) and tag/`release` events unaffected — regression-pinned.
- [ ] ci.yml comment block updated: the schedule is the release arming mechanism, empty ticks short-circuit.

Context: #1537 (post-merge main CI retirement), #1538 (slim nightly), ci.yml `schedule:` + `release` job comments.
